must_remember: Electric potential $V$ is a scalar quantity defined as work done per unit positive test charge: $V = W/q_0$.
The electric field is the negative gradient of the electric potential: $\vec{E} = -\vec{\nabla} V$.
Electric field lines are always normal (perpendicular) to equipotential surfaces at every point.
No work is done in moving a test charge between two points located on the same equipotential surface.
The potential inside a charged conducting spherical shell is constant and equal to the potential at its surface: $V = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{Q}{R}$.
Electrostatic force is conservative, meaning work done depends only on the initial and final positions, not on the path.

glossary.meaning: The work done by an external agent per unit positive test charge in bringing it from infinity to a point without acceleration.
A surface on which the electric potential is constant at every point.
The total work done in assembling a system of charges from infinity to their current configuration.
A vector quantity defined as the product of the magnitude of either charge and the distance between them, directed from negative to positive charge.
